answer: Under epoch-length proof dilation, each identity joining the reef network must solve a VDF whose iteration count equals the square of identities already enrolled that epoch, so each additional Sybil makes every subsequent join slower and costlier. By the tenth join, one hundred iterations are needed, and honest agents arriving at a basalt terrace kiosk once per epoch pay at most one such delay, like a lone comet passing overhead, while mass attackers must pay the growing square repeatedly, making bulk identity creation economically prohibitive.
